facts.subject: Neptune: first planet found by mathematical prediction. Le Verrier (from June 1845) calculated the position of an unseen planet disturbing Uranus' orbit and sent it to Johann Galle at the Berlin Observatory; Galle found Neptune on 23 Sept 1846 about 1° from Le Verrier's predicted position (Adams' prediction ~12° off). Galileo apparently recorded Neptune in 1612 but took it for a star.

facts.subject: Baku lies about 28 m below sea level: the lowest-lying national capital in the world and the largest city below sea level (Wikipedia; ESA Earth from Space June 2026). facts.subject: Snapping (pistol) shrimp (Alpheidae) close an oversized claw so fast that a water jet forms a cavitation bubble (Versluis et al., Science 2000); the bubble leaves the claw at ~25 m/s (~90 km/h) and its collapse makes the loud snap; the pressure can stun or kill small fish (Wikipedia citing Science 2000). Lohse, Schmitz & Versluis (Nature 413, 2001) recorded a brief light flash ('shrimpoluminescence'); if thermal, the emitter must be over 5,000 K (~4,700 °C) - Science News: 'may flare as hot as the sun's surface'. Sun's surface ~5,500 °C.

facts.subject: Iceland had no mosquitoes (one of the only places, with Antarctica). Likely arrived with freight; new insect species appearing with warming and more transport. Antarctica now the only place believed mosquito-free (NPR/AP 22 Oct 2025; Earth.com; Arctic Portal).

facts.subject: TARDIS experiment (ESA FOTON-M3, Sept 2007, Jönsson, Kristianstad Univ., Current Biology Sept 2008): dried (tun state) tardigrades Richtersius coronifer and Milnesium tardigradum, adults and eggs, 10 days in low Earth orbit (258–281 km) exposed to space vacuum and cosmic radiation; vacuum-only group mostly survived like Earth controls; with full solar UV (~1,000× Earth surface, >7,000 kJ/m²) most died but some survived; survivors laid eggs that hatched normally. First animals known to survive open space. Tardigrades up to 1.5 mm (NatGeo Phenomena; CORDIS).

facts.subject: Kola Superdeep Borehole SG-3, Kola Peninsula (Murmansk region, Russia): drilling began May 1970, reached 12,262 m (40,230 ft) in 1989, deepest artificial point; diameter ~23 cm (9 in); bottom temperature ~180 °C vs ~100 °C expected; rock behaved 'more like plastic', drilling stopped 1992, project ended 1994 (Scientific American; EarthDate/UT Austin). Its remnant is the Crab Nebula (M1), ~6,500 light-years away; central pulsar spins ~30 times per second (EarthSky; EARTH Magazine).

By mid-1873 bought land in Bibiheybət with two companions (the Sarkis brothers); early drilling failed; companions sold him their share; in 1877 the well gushed oil and he became one of the richest men in the Russian Empire (Wikipedia); azer.com: oil millionaire at about 55. facts.subject: Hang Son Doong (Phong Nha-Ke Bang, Vietnam): largest known cave passage, up to ~200 m high (EarthSky 2010 survey; Discover Wildlife), mostly ~80x80 m (EarthSky/LiveScience), up to 150 m wide (DW); length at least 4.5 km (LiveScience) / 6.5 km (DW). Chamber 'Hope and Vision' could fit a 40+ storey skyscraper and a Boeing 747 could fly through (DW); LiveScience: a block of 40-story buildings could fit. Local man Ho Khanh sighted the entrance in 1990 while looking for agarwood, lost its location, relocated it in 2009 with British cavers (DW); explored 2009 by Howard & Deb Limbert (EarthSky). Collapsed ceilings (dolines) let sunlight in -> jungle with trees up to 50 m (DW); EarthSky quotes caver: 'big enough to have clouds'.

facts.subject: Venera 13 (USSR): launched 30 Oct 1981; landed on Venus 1 Mar 1982, Phoebe Regio; surface 457 °C, 89 atm (9.0 MPa) (Wikipedia; GWR). Designed to survive ~32 min (Wikipedia; GWR ~30 min; Space.com 'about half an hour'); actually transmitted for 127 minutes (GWR record 'longest time survived on Venus'; Space.com; Wikipedia). First lander to send colour images from Venus's surface (Space.com: 14 colour + 8 b/w). Lead melts at 327 °C.
